solver_summary: I could verify only the denominator-clearing part: for each k, (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k = \prod_{j=1}^k (1-q^(2dj)) = (q^d;q^d)_k \prod_{j=1}^k (1+q^(dj)), so after multiplying the k-th summand of T_{d,r,n}(q) by U_{d,n}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^(dj)), all denominator factors are cancelled because k\le n-1. Hence G_{d,r,n}(q)=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) is indeed a Laurent polynomial. However, the substantive claim that M_n(q)=[n]_q\Phi_n(q)^2 divides this Laurent polynomial is exactly the deep q-congruence/theorem-level content, and no admissible trusted declaration or lemma establishing that divisibility was provided.
